Ben / Laura / Sarah — thanks for the ping. I skimmed the Helix redlines and flagged the key risk areas. Below are practical options we can offer; each balances Helix's need for protection with Redwood's desire to keep a finite exposure: 

Option A (narrow monetary sub-cap): Carve out confidentiality breaches and trade-secret misappropriation from the general contract cap, but subject those categories to a specific sub-cap equal to 2x the annualized subscription fees for the affected year (or $5M, whichever is greater). That creates a predictable limit while recognizing the seriousness of IP breaches.

Option B (indemnity + specific remedies): Keep the general liability cap but add an indemnity for willful misappropriation of trade secrets and a clause requiring Redwood to: (i) pay documented third-party costs to remediate loss, and (ii) cooperate with injunctive relief. Monetary damages remain capped, but indemnity for third-party claims is carved out.

Option C (mutual unlimited carve-out narrow scope): Make the confidentiality/trade secret carve-out mutual and limited to direct damages for proven willful misappropriation where injunctive relief is not an adequate remedy. This keeps the door open to uncapped remedies in the narrowest conceivable circumstances but requires a high evidentiary bar.

Draft redline snippet I can circulate if you prefer one of the above. My recommendation: start with Option A (monetary sub-cap) — it’s easier for procurement and keeps exposure bounded.

See attached quick snippet and rationale.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Commercial & Privacy | Redwood Inference
